narrative.intro: Lawrence Livermore National Security obligated $3.4B in FY2026 to date, from a single award with an average award size of $3.4B. Obligations fell 5.4% year over year. The FY trend shows a rise from $2.8B in FY21 and $2.8B in FY22, to $3B in FY23, $3.2B in FY24, $3.6B in FY25, and then $3.4B in FY26. The current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date obligations rather than full-year totals. The vendor-level picture is concentrated: one award accounts for the entire FY2026 to date obligation total, so changes to that single contract drive the supplier’s year-to-date totals. The note that award-value figures in largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables are total contract values indicates that some reported award numbers may reflect full contract value rather than fiscal-year obligations. For contractors and procurement analysts, the combination of a single large award and a small year-over-year decline highlights sensitivity to contract timing and one-off award events when assessing near-term revenue exposure.
